analysis.title: Intelligence weekly #135: Can Chinese hyperscaler earn an attractive return on AI capex?
key_insights: UBS CIO's base case is that China AI infrastructure earns roughly 12-20% ROIC with a cash payback of about 2.5-3 years. Returns stay below the US mainly because comparable computing hardware costs more in China.
Owned GPU rental earns about 12% ROIC. Owned model services (Model-as-a-Service, MaaS) reach roughly 19-20%, because the provider sells model access and not only computing time.
In the owned GPU rental case, CNY 10 million of server capex and about CNY 310,000 of monthly rental revenue give a 44% operating margin, a 12% ROIC and a 3.2-year cash payback.

The MaaS base case assumes 4,200 tokens per second per GPU, a 50% inference mix and blended pricing of CNY 9 per million tokens. It yields a 76% gross margin, a 53% operating margin, about 19% ROIC and a 2.6-year payback.

Renting servers from a third party (the asset-light model) assumes a customer price of CNY 250,000 a month against a compute rental cost of CNY 200,000. That gives about a 20% operating margin, with no upfront server investment and immediate cash generation.

The same owned GPU rental business normally earns over 30% ROIC in the US. Higher server cost in China raises depreciation and enlarges the invested-capital denominator, and lower electricity and data center costs do not fully offset it.
The report says better model efficiency can narrow China's operating-profit gap but cannot close the ROIC gap unless hardware cost also falls.

The main upside driver is utilization: a higher inference mix, higher token throughput, stable revenue per unit of compute and lower server costs. The report says a lower-priced but efficient model can out-earn an expensive model that uses too much compute.

UBS would stay constructive while three conditions hold: advanced capacity stays highly utilized, paid inference becomes a larger share of usage, and revenue per unit of compute is stable or improves.
UBS expects a rational provider to own core capacity for strategic customers and steady demand, and to rent incremental capacity for peak demand or uncertain workloads.

Effective 1 November 2026, UBS CIO no longer rates or ranks equities as Most Preferred, Bellwether or Least Preferred. It now designates stocks as 'CIO Selected', which is not a rating and sets no CIO price target.
The AI Equity Selection List history shows Alibaba and Tencent moved to Most Preferred on 8 Jul 2026. Both were also added to the China AI Platforms list on 1 Oct 2026.

sector_views.rationale: Constructive but not unconditional. Base-case ROIC of 12-20% with a 2.5-3 year payback is attractive if demand is durable and the equipment stays economically useful.

risk_factors: Utilization supported mainly by internal training rather than paying external customers would weaken the return case.
Chinese cloud providers pay materially more for advanced computing hardware, and AI monetization is at an earlier stage than in the US.
Equipment obsolescence and flexibility risk when owning servers, versus the lower margin from renting capacity.

Per company risk table: Alibaba faces macroeconomic headwinds in China and intensified competition. Tencent faces a faster-than-expected slowdown in PC game revenues, aggressive subsidy and marketing spend, and disruptive competitor products.

tension_points.bull_case: A 12-20% ROIC with a 2.5-3 year payback is attractive. Returns can rise with a higher inference mix, better token throughput, stable revenue per unit of compute and lower server costs, and China's AI sector has more room to improve than the US.
tension_points.bear_case: Returns sit below the US (over 30% for owned GPU rental versus about 12% in China) because Chinese firms pay more for servers and allocate less capacity to revenue-generating inference. Monetization is at an earlier stage.
tension_points.what_invalidates: UBS would become more cautious if utilization is supported mainly by internal training rather than paying external customers.

theme_stances.key_argument: China can earn attractive returns from AI infrastructure despite a hardware-cost disadvantage, if utilization and paid inference mix improve.
theme_stances.evidence: China AI infrastructure can still generate attractive returns
